indication.text: ELUCIREM is a gadolinium-based contrast agent indicated in adult and pediatric patients aged 2 years and older for use with MRI to detect and visualize lesions with abnormal vascularity in the central nervous system (brain, spine, and associated tissues) and the body (head and neck, thorax, abdomen, pelvis, and musculoskeletal system).

citations.quote: ELUCIREM is a gadolinium-based contrast agent indicated in adult and pediatric patients aged 2 years and older for use with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to detect and visualize lesions with abnormal vascularity in:

- the central nervous system (brain, spine, and associated tissues),
- the body (head and neck, thorax, abdomen, pelvis, and musculoskeletal system).

target_moa.text: Gadopiclenol is a nonionic, macrocyclic gadolinium complex that alters the relaxation rates of hydrogen nuclei in water, changing signal intensity on T1-weighted MRI in a concentration-dependent manner; it has higher relaxivity than currently marketed GBCAs, allowing use at a lower dose.

citations.quote: It is a nonionic, macrocyclic gadolinium (Gd) complex that alters the relaxation rates of hydrogen nuclei in water and thereby changes signal intensity on T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in a concentration dependent manner.
As further detailed in Section 6.3.1, gadopiclenol has higher measured relaxivity than currently marketed GBCAs, which allows use of a lower dose.

modality.text: Small molecule (macrocyclic gadolinium-based contrast agent / metal chelate).

description.text: Extended existing indications to pediatric patients under 2 years of age, including term neonates

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application updates the U.S. Prescribing Information to include an extension of the existing Elucirem indications to pediatric patients < 2 years of age, including term neonates. In addition, this supplement provides for revisions to subsection 8.1 Pregnancy to reflect clinical experience regarding the risk of in utero exposure to gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs) based on a review of scientific literature.
